lines.li: [them] So you're from the colony our people married into.
[us] I suppose we are, since the wedding.
[them,their:tribal] Then sit by me, our fire is open to your people now.
[them,their:empire] A connection by marriage, yes, though not a close one.
[them] Then you'll forgive me for asking a lot of questions.
[them] We heard you had raiders at your walls.
[us] We did, and we're still here.
[them] Next time, send word, our people will come for yours.
[us] Thank your people for the gifts that keep coming each season.
[them,their:tribal] It is how our camp remembers yours, each season, by the moons.
[them,their:medieval] It's custom, though the town reeve grumbles about the cost.
[them,their:industrial] It's expected, and it keeps the road busy.
[them] It's what bound peoples do.
[them] Our people hold the wrong against your colony, and I'll lead them one day.
[us] Is there no way to set it down?
[them] Not one I've been told of.
[them] If our people ever make a match of this, I'd want it done properly.
[us] Then I'll speak for it properly, when you're ready.
[them,their:lowtech] Not yet, the old ones need to get used to your face first.
[them] Not yet, let me tell my people first.
[us] What do your people expect of a colony they're bound to by marriage?
[them,their:tribal] A place at the fire when we visit, and help with the hunt when we ask.
[them,their:medieval] A seat at the table, a gift at midwinter, and no arguing with the old ones.
[them,their:industrial] A letter now and then, and help when the caravan breaks down.
[them,their:empire] Correct forms of address, and attendance when it is asked for.
[them,their:spacer,!their:empire] Courtesy, and that you keep your records straight.
[them] To be remembered, mostly.
[us] We can manage that.
[them] The Empire signs no pacts, but a titled household remembers a colony it married into.
[us] We'll try to be worth remembering.
[them] We heard about {DEAD}, and our people grieve with yours.
[us] Thank you, it helps to hear it from a people bound to us.
[them] Our peoples were bound once, through that marriage.
[us] We could be again, if both sides wanted it.
[them] Maybe, but not this year.
[us] Do your people keep a bond once the marriage that made it is over?
[them,their:lowtech] The bond was the two of them, the elders say, and it went with them.
[them,their:hightech] The terms ended with the marriage, as terms do.
[them] Not by right, but people remember who treated them well.
